newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan three-month NCDs average yield at 6.753 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan three-month NCDs average yield at 6.753 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank on Monday issued T$11 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit at an average yield of 6.753 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the bids was between 6.50 and 6.90 percent and demand totalled T$11.3 billion.

The issue was seen by analysts as an effort to take absorb some liquidity and take some of the fire out of a renewed bull run in Taiwan's stock market bull run, where the index has pushed to a series of seven-year highs in recent weeks.
Monday was no exception, with the index gaining 64.21 points or 0.69 percent to a seven-year high close of 9,322.84 -- despite a morning announcement of the injection.
Taiwan's overnight and short-term money rates soared into double digits in late June as investors diverted holdings into the share market.
Likewise, investors have been liquidating their foreign exchange holdings into Taiwan dollars, bolstering the local currency and halting what had been a slow, steady devaluation.

The central bank repeatedly issued NCDs when the index was hottest in March and April, a move widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts said was fuelling the dramatic rally.
The central bank has confirmed that it was responding to the liquidity sitution but denied that it was acting directly in response to the stock market bull run.
